newsitem.title: USA: Former UPI, FNN chairman sentenced to federal prison.
newsitem.headline: Former UPI, FNN chairman sentenced to federal prison.

text.p: The former chairman of United Press International and Financial News Network was sentenced on Tuesday to 57 months in federal prison for conspiracy, bank fraud and securities fraud.
Earl Brian, who was convicted last October of 10 counts, was also fined $25,000 and U.S. District Court Judge Ronald Lew ordered him to surrender to authorities Aug. 18 to begin serving his sentence.

In the late 1980s and early 1990's, Brian, 55, was chairman and CEO of UPI and FNN, both of which were controlled by Infotechnology Inc. Evidence introduced in his trial showed Brian conspired to conceal the companies' declining financial health to obtain more than $70 million in bank loans in 1989.
Brian served as California Gov. Ronald Reagan's secretary for health and welfare from 1972-74 and later unsuccessfully sought the state Republican nomination for the U.S. Senate.
Steven Bolen, the former Chief Financial Officer of FNN and Gary Prince, who held the same position at UPI, previously pleaded guilty to similar charges and are scheduled to be sentenced in August.
